source.text: Κατήντησεν δὲ καὶ εἰς Δέρβην καὶ εἰς Λύστραν.

records.literal_gloss: He came down then also to Derbe and to Lystra.

en.L: And he came also to Derbe and to Lystra.
en.B: Paul came to Derbe and then on to Lystra.
en.R: Paul traveled to the town of Derbe and then to Lystra.

es.L: Y llegó también a Derbe y a Listra.
es.B: Pablo llegó a Derbe y luego a Listra.
es.R: Pablo viajó a la ciudad de Derbe y después a Listra.

sw.L: Na akafika pia Derbe na Listra.
sw.B: Paulo alifika Derbe, kisha akaenda Listra.
sw.R: Paulo alisafiri mpaka mji wa Derbe, kisha mpaka Listra.

decisions.choice: he: Paul, travelling with Silas
decisions.reason: The verb is singular and follows 15:40-41, where Paul chooses Silas and goes through Syria and Cilicia. Paul is the leader, so the story follows him.

decisions.choice: Derbe and Lystra: towns of Lycaonia that Paul had visited before
decisions.reason: Paul and Barnabas preached in both towns on their first journey (14:6-21). Coming overland from Cilicia, a traveler reaches Derbe first, which is why the order is the reverse of chapter 14.

decisions.choice: Paul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject, which the Greek leaves to the context.

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says what Derbe was.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ μαθητής τις ἦν ἐκεῖ ὀνόματι Τιμόθεος, υἱὸς γυναικὸς Ἰουδαίας πιστῆς, πατρὸς δὲ Ἕλληνος, ὃς ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Λύστροις καὶ Ἰκονίῳ ἀδελφῶν·

records.literal_gloss: And behold a disciple certain was there by name Timothy, son of a woman Jewish believing, of a father but Greek, \v 2 who was being well spoken of by the in Lystra and Iconium brothers;

en.L: And look, a certain disciple was there named Timothy, [the] son of a believing Jewish woman, but of a Greek father, \v 2 who was well spoken of by the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in Lystra and Iconium.
en.B: A disciple called Timothy was living there. His mother was a Jewish woman who believed, but his father was a Greek. \v 2 The {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in Lystra and Iconium thought highly of him.
en.R: A follower of Jesus named Timothy lived there. His mother was Jewish, and she believed in Jesus. But his father was not Jewish. He was a Greek. \v 2 The {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in Lystra and Iconium said good things about Timothy.

es.L: Y mira, había allí un discípulo llamado Timoteo, hijo de una mujer judía creyente, pero de padre griego, \v 2 del cual daban buen testimonio los hermanos de Listra e Iconio.
es.B: Allí vivía un discípulo llamado Timoteo. Su madre era una judía creyente, pero su padre era griego. \v 2 Los hermanos de Listra e Iconio hablaban muy bien de él.
es.R: Allí vivía un discípulo de Jesús que se llamaba Timoteo. Su madre era judía y creía en Jesús. Pero su padre no era judío; era griego. \v 2 Los hermanos de Listra y de Iconio decían cosas buenas de Timoteo.

sw.L: Na tazama, palikuwa na mwanafunzi mmoja huko jina lake Timotheo, mwana wa mwanamke Myahudi aliyeamini, lakini [mwana] wa baba Mgiriki, \v 2 ambaye alishuhudiwa vema na ndugu waliokuwa Listra na Ikonio.
sw.B: Huko kulikuwa na mwanafunzi mmoja aitwaye Timotheo. Mama yake alikuwa Myahudi aliyeamini, lakini baba yake alikuwa Mgiriki. \v 2 Ndugu wa Listra na Ikonio walimshuhudia kuwa mtu mwema.
sw.R: Huko aliishi mwanafunzi wa Yesu aitwaye Timotheo. Mama yake alikuwa Myahudi, naye alimwamini Yesu. Lakini baba yake hakuwa Myahudi; alikuwa Mgiriki. \v 2 Ndugu wa Listra na Ikonio walisema mambo mazuri kuhusu Timotheo.

decisions.choice: there: most likely Lystra
decisions.reason: Lystra is the last place named, and the believers who speak well of Timothy are those of Lystra and Iconium (16:2). Paul later recalls his sufferings at Lystra, which Timothy knew about (2 Timothy 3:11).

decisions.choice: a believing Jewish mother and a Greek father: a mixed family
decisions.reason: A Greek here means a Gentile, not necessarily someone from Greece. Timothy's mother and grandmother, Eunice and Lois, taught him the Scriptures from childhood (2 Timothy 1:5, 3:15). The father is never said to have believed.

decisions.choice: well spoken of: known and approved by others
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the seven in 6:3: other people vouch for him.

decisions.choice: brothers: the believers, men and women
decisions.reason: The word is used for the whole community of believers in those towns.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that calls attention to what follows, in current wording rather than an old one.

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word takes in all the believers, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: she believed in Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what she believed: she was a disciple, like her son.

decisions.choice: discípulo (every level); discípulo de Jesús (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet word for Acts, recorded once in this chapter: "discípulo" at every level, even where the English Readable says "follower", so the same word runs through the book. Readable adds "de Jesús", as the English does.

decisions.choice: hermanos, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "brothers and sisters". Spanish "hermanos" already takes in the women among the believers (meaning decision m4), so the setting has no second wording to switch to. The same in verse 40.

decisions.choice: mwanafunzi (every level); mwanafunzi wa Yesu (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet word for Acts, recorded once in this chapter: "mwanafunzi" at every level, even where the English Readable says "follower", so the same word runs through the book. Readable adds "wa Yesu", as the English does.

decisions.choice: ndugu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "brothers and sisters". Swahili "ndugu" already means believers, men and women (meaning decision m4), so the setting has nothing to change. The same in verse 40.

source.text: τοῦτον ἠθέλησεν ὁ Παῦλος σὺν αὐτῷ ἐξελθεῖν, καὶ λαβὼν περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν διὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς ὄντας ἐν τοῖς τόποις ἐκείνοις, ᾔδεισαν γὰρ ἅπαντες ὅτι Ἕλλην ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ ὑπῆρχεν.

records.literal_gloss: This one wanted the Paul with him to go forth, and having taken he circumcised him because of the Jews the being in the places those; they knew for all that a Greek the father of him was.

en.L: Paul wanted this one to go out with him, and taking [him], he circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
en.B: Paul wanted to have Timothy with him when he set out. With the Jews of that area in mind, he took him and circumcised him, since all of them knew that his father was a Greek.
en.R: Paul wanted Timothy to travel with him. The Jews who lived there all knew that Timothy's father was a Greek. So Paul circumcised Timothy, so that those Jews would not have a reason to refuse to listen to them.

es.L: Pablo quiso que este saliera con él, y tomándolo, lo circuncidó a causa de los judíos que estaban en aquellos lugares, porque todos sabían que su padre era griego.
es.B: Pablo quería llevar a Timoteo consigo en el viaje. Teniendo en cuenta a los judíos de aquella región, lo tomó y lo circuncidó, porque todos sabían que su padre era griego.
es.R: Pablo quería que Timoteo viajara con él. Todos los judíos de aquel lugar sabían que el padre de Timoteo era griego. Por eso Pablo circuncidó a Timoteo, para que esos judíos no tuvieran una razón para negarse a escucharlos.

sw.L: Paulo alitaka huyu atoke pamoja naye, na akamchukua akamtahiri kwa sababu ya Wayahudi waliokuwa katika sehemu zile, kwa maana wote walijua kwamba baba yake alikuwa Mgiriki.
sw.B: Paulo alitaka Timotheo aende pamoja naye safarini. Kwa ajili ya Wayahudi wa eneo lile, alimchukua akamtahiri, kwa sababu wote walijua kwamba baba yake alikuwa Mgiriki.
sw.R: Paulo alitaka Timotheo asafiri pamoja naye. Wayahudi wote walioishi huko walijua kwamba baba yake Timotheo alikuwa Mgiriki. Basi Paulo akamtahiri Timotheo, ili Wayahudi hao wasipate sababu ya kukataa kuwasikiliza.

decisions.choice: circumcised: given the sign of God's covenant with Abraham's family
decisions.reason: God gave circumcision to Abraham and his descendants as the sign of the covenant (Genesis 17:10-14). Every Jewish boy was circumcised on the eighth day (Luke 1:59, 2:21). With a Gentile father, Timothy had not been.

decisions.choice: because of the Jews: Timothy, with a Jewish mother, would be seen by them as a Jew who had not kept the law
alternatives: they would see him only as a Gentile
decisions.reason: Everyone knew his father was a Greek, so everyone knew he was uncircumcised. Whether a child of a Jewish mother was then counted a Jew is not certain; the later rabbinic rule says so, but how far it held in Paul's day is unclear. Either way, an uncircumcised companion with a Jewish mother would have closed synagogue doors to Paul.

decisions.choice: not a condition of salvation: done so that the message could be heard
alternatives: Paul going back on the Jerusalem decision
decisions.reason: The Jerusalem meeting had just decided that Gentiles need not be circumcised to be saved (15:1-29), and Paul refused to have Titus, a Greek, circumcised (Galatians 2:3). Timothy's case is different because of his Jewish mother, and Paul says he became like a Jew to win Jews (1 Corinthians 9:20).

decisions.choice: with the Jews of that area in mind
alternatives: because of the Jews who were in those places
decisions.reason: Balanced brings the reason forward, so that the sentence does not end on the reason for the reason.

decisions.choice: so that those Jews would not have a reason to refuse to listen to them
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why the Jews mattered, as the meaning notes explain. The text itself gives only "because of the Jews".

source.text: ὡς δὲ διεπορεύοντο τὰς πόλεις, παρεδίδοσαν αὐτοῖς φυλάσσειν τὰ δόγματα τὰ κεκριμένα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τῶν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις.

records.literal_gloss: As then they were passing through the cities, they were delivering to them to keep the decrees the having been decided by the apostles and elders the in Jerusalem.

en.L: And as they went through the cities, they delivered to them the decrees decided on by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem, for [them] to keep.
en.B: As they made their way from town to town, they passed on to the believers the decisions reached by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem, for them to observe.
en.R: They traveled from town to town. In each place they told the believers what the apostles and elders in Jerusalem had decided, and they told them to obey these rules.

es.L: Y conforme pasaban por las ciudades, les transmitían, para que [los] guardaran, los decretos decididos por los apóstoles y ancianos que estaban en Jerusalén.
es.B: Mientras iban de ciudad en ciudad, transmitían a los creyentes las decisiones que habían tomado los apóstoles y los ancianos de Jerusalén, para que las cumplieran.
es.R: Viajaban de ciudad en ciudad. En cada lugar les contaban a los creyentes lo que habían decidido los apóstoles y los líderes de la iglesia de Jerusalén, y les decían que obedecieran esas reglas.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakipita katika miji, waliwakabidhi maagizo yaliyoamuliwa na mitume na wazee waliokuwa Yerusalemu, [ili] wayashike.
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakienda kutoka mji mmoja hadi mwingine, waliwapa waumini maamuzi yaliyofanywa na mitume na wazee wa Yerusalemu, ili wayafuate.
sw.R: Walisafiri kutoka mji mmoja hadi mwingine. Katika kila mahali waliwaeleza waumini yale ambayo mitume na viongozi wa kanisa huko Yerusalemu walikuwa wameamua, wakawaambia wayatii maagizo hayo.

decisions.choice: decrees: the formal decisions of the Jerusalem meeting
decisions.reason: The word is used for official decisions and decrees (Luke 2:1). Here it means the ruling of 15:28-29: Gentile believers should keep away from food offered to idols, from blood, from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality.

decisions.choice: to them: the believers in the cities
decisions.reason: The letter of 15:23 was addressed to Gentile believers, and 16:5 goes on to speak of the churches.

decisions.choice: went through, delivered: something they did again and again
decisions.reason: Both verbs are imperfect, for repeated action: in each town they did the same.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people meant, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: ancianos (L, B); líderes de la iglesia (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering for the elders as a church office, recorded once in this chapter. At Readable "ancianos" would sound like old men in general, so it names their role; the English Readable keeps "elders", which English readers know as a church office.

decisions.choice: wazee (L, B); viongozi wa kanisa (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering for the elders as a church office, recorded once in this chapter. At Readable "wazee" would be heard as old men in general, so it names their role; the English Readable keeps "elders", which English readers know as a church office.

source.text: αἱ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησίαι ἐστερεοῦντο τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐπερίσσευον τῷ ἀριθμῷ καθ’ ἡμέραν.

records.literal_gloss: The indeed therefore churches were being strengthened in the faith and were increasing in the number every day.

en.L: So the churches were being strengthened in the faith and were increasing in number every day.
en.B: So the churches grew firmer in the faith, and their numbers rose day by day.
en.R: So the churches grew stronger in their faith, and more people joined them every day.

es.L: Así pues, las iglesias se fortalecían en la fe y crecían en número cada día.
es.B: Así las iglesias se afirmaban en la fe, y su número aumentaba día tras día.
es.R: Así las iglesias se hacían más fuertes en su fe, y cada día se les unía más gente.

sw.L: Basi makanisa yalikuwa yakiimarishwa katika imani na kuongezeka idadi kila siku.
sw.B: Basi makanisa yaliimarika katika imani, na idadi yao ikaongezeka siku kwa siku.
sw.R: Basi makanisa yalizidi kuwa imara katika imani yao, na kila siku watu zaidi walijiunga nayo.

decisions.choice: the faith: the believers' trust in Jesus, held in common
decisions.reason: The word has the article, as in 6:7 and 14:22, where it is the faith shared by all who believe. Its first sense is trust; the article does not turn it into a list of doctrines.

decisions.choice: so: a summary that closes a section
alternatives: the result of the decrees only
decisions.reason: Luke marks the end of a stage of the story with a short report of growth, as in 6:7, 9:31 and 12:24.

decisions.choice: more people joined them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the growth in number meant.

source.text: Διῆλθον δὲ τὴν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν, κωλυθέντες ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ἐλθόντες δὲ κατὰ τὴν Μυσίαν ἐπείραζον εἰς τὴν Βιθυνίαν πορευθῆναι καὶ οὐκ εἴασεν αὐτοὺς τὸ πνεῦμα Ἰησοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: They passed through then the Phrygian and Galatian region, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in the Asia; \v 7 having come then to the Mysia they were trying into the Bithynia to go, and not allowed them the Spirit of Jesus;

en.L: And they went through the Phrygian and Galatian region, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia. \v 7 And when they came up to Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them.
en.B: They went on through the Phrygian and Galatian country, because the Holy Spirit had stopped them from speaking the word in Asia. \v 7 Coming as far as Mysia, they made an attempt to go on into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not permit it.
en.R: Then they went through the area of Phrygia and Galatia. The Holy Spirit did not let them tell God's message in the province of Asia. \v 7 When they came near Mysia, they tried to go north into Bithynia. But the Spirit of Jesus did not let them go there.

es.L: Y atravesaron la región frigia y gálata, impedidos por el Espíritu Santo de hablar la palabra en Asia. \v 7 Y al llegar a la altura de Misia, intentaban ir a Bitinia, y el Espíritu de Jesús no se lo permitió.
es.B: Atravesaron la región de Frigia y Galacia, porque el Espíritu Santo les había impedido predicar la palabra en Asia. \v 7 Al llegar a la frontera de Misia, intentaron pasar a Bitinia, pero el Espíritu de Jesús no se lo permitió.
es.R: Luego pasaron por la región de Frigia y Galacia. El Espíritu Santo no les dejó anunciar el mensaje de Dios en la provincia de Asia. \v 7 Cuando llegaron cerca de Misia, intentaron ir hacia el norte, a Bitinia. Pero el Espíritu de Jesús no los dejó ir allí.

sw.L: Na wakapita katika eneo la Frigia na Galatia, wakiwa wamezuiwa na Roho Mtakatifu kunena neno katika Asia. \v 7 Na walipofika karibu na Misia, walijaribu kwenda Bithinia, na Roho wa Yesu hakuwaruhusu.
sw.B: Walipita katika eneo la Frigia na Galatia, kwa kuwa Roho Mtakatifu alikuwa amewazuia wasihubiri neno katika Asia. \v 7 Walipofika mpakani mwa Misia, walijaribu kuingia Bithinia, lakini Roho wa Yesu hakuwaruhusu.
sw.R: Kisha walipita katika eneo la Frigia na Galatia. Roho Mtakatifu hakuwaruhusu kuhubiri ujumbe wa Mungu katika jimbo la Asia. \v 7 Walipofika karibu na Misia, walijaribu kwenda kaskazini mpaka Bithinia. Lakini Roho wa Yesu hakuwaruhusu kwenda huko.

decisions.choice: the Phrygian and Galatian region: one area that was both Phrygian and Galatian
alternatives: two areas, Phrygia and the region of Galatia
decisions.reason: One article governs both words, and Phrygian can be an adjective, which suggests a single area: the part of Phrygia that lay in the Roman province of Galatia, where Iconium and Pisidian Antioch were. The words can also be read as two areas.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey
decisions.reason: Its chief city was Ephesus. Paul worked there later for over two years (19:1-10).

decisions.choice: having been forbidden: the Spirit's leading came before or during this stage of the journey
alternatives: the reason they went to Phrygia, stated as a fact
decisions.reason: The participle is aorist. It may tell why they took this route, or what happened on it. Luke does not say how the Spirit spoke, whether through a prophet, a vision or events.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Jesus: the Holy Spirit, who is also the Spirit of Jesus
decisions.reason: The same Spirit is named in 16:6 and 16:7. Only here is he called the Spirit of Jesus; compare "the Spirit of Christ" (Romans 8:9), "the Spirit of Jesus Christ" (Philippians 1:19) and "the Spirit of his Son" (Galatians 4:6). The risen Jesus pours out the Spirit (2:33) and leads his people by him.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "the Spirit of Jesus"
alternatives: some later manuscripts read only "the Spirit"
decisions.reason: The early manuscripts have "the Spirit of Jesus"; later ones, followed by the King James Version, leave out "of Jesus". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: came up to Mysia: reached its border
decisions.reason: The preposition means opposite or over against. They came to the edge of Mysia, in the northwest, and tried to turn northeast.

decisions.choice: the province of Asia; go north
decisions.reason: Readable says that Asia was a province, not the continent, and which way Bithynia lay.

decisions.choice: tell God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word was, as at 6:2.

decisions.choice: la región frigia y gálata (L); la región de Frigia y Galacia (B, R)
alternatives: Frigia y la región de Galacia
decisions.reason: The Greek joins two adjectives to one noun, most likely one area that was both Phrygian and Galatian (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the two adjectives; Balanced and Readable keep a single "región" so that it is not read as two separate places.

decisions.choice: eneo la Frigia na Galatia (every level)
alternatives: nchi ya Frigia na nchi ya Galatia
decisions.reason: Most likely one area that was both Phrygian and Galatian (meaning decision m1). Swahili has no adjectives for these names, so every level uses one noun, "eneo", with both names after it, which keeps it a single region.

source.text: παρελθόντες δὲ τὴν Μυσίαν κατέβησαν εἰς Τρῳάδα.

records.literal_gloss: Having passed by then the Mysia they came down to Troas.

en.L: And passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.
en.B: So they skirted Mysia and went down to Troas.
en.R: So they went along the edge of Mysia and came down to the city of Troas, on the coast.

es.L: Y pasando de largo por Misia, bajaron a Troas.
es.B: Así que bordearon Misia y bajaron a Troas.
es.R: Entonces pasaron por el borde de Misia y bajaron hasta la ciudad de Troas, en la costa.

sw.L: Na wakiisha kupita Misia, walishuka mpaka Troa.
sw.B: Basi walipita kando ya Misia, wakashuka mpaka Troa.
sw.R: Basi walipita pembeni mwa Misia, wakashuka mpaka mji wa Troa, ulio pwani.

decisions.choice: passing by: going through without stopping to preach
decisions.reason: Troas itself lay in Mysia, so they must have crossed it. The verb means they did not stay or work there.

decisions.choice: Troas: a port on the Aegean coast, near ancient Troy
decisions.reason: Alexandria Troas was a Roman colony and the usual port for sailing from Asia to Macedonia. Paul passed through it again (20:5-12; 2 Corinthians 2:12).

decisions.choice: the city of; on the coast
decisions.reason: Readable says what Troas was, since the next step is a sea voyage.

source.text: καὶ ὅραμα διὰ νυκτὸς τῷ Παύλῳ ὤφθη, ἀνὴρ Μακεδών τις ἦν ἑστὼς καὶ παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων· Διαβὰς εἰς Μακεδονίαν βοήθησον ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And a vision during night to the Paul appeared: a man Macedonian certain was standing and urging him and saying, Having crossed over into Macedonia help us.

en.L: And a vision appeared to Paul during [the] night: a certain Macedonian man was standing and urging him and saying, "Cross over into Macedonia [and] help us."
en.B: In the night Paul saw a vision. A man of Macedonia stood there and pleaded with him, "Cross over to Macedonia and help us!"
en.R: That night God showed Paul a vision. In it a man from Macedonia was standing and begging him, "Come across the sea to Macedonia and help us!"

es.L: Y una visión se le apareció a Pablo durante [la] noche: un hombre macedonio estaba de pie, rogándole y diciendo: «Pasa a Macedonia [y] ayúdanos».
es.B: Por la noche Pablo tuvo una visión: un hombre de Macedonia estaba allí de pie y le suplicaba: «¡Pasa a Macedonia y ayúdanos!».
es.R: Esa noche Dios le mostró una visión a Pablo. En ella, un hombre de Macedonia estaba de pie y le rogaba: «¡Cruza el mar, ven a Macedonia y ayúdanos!».

sw.L: Na maono yalimtokea Paulo wakati wa usiku: mtu mmoja Mmakedonia alikuwa amesimama akimsihi na kusema, "Vuka mpaka Makedonia, utusaidie."
sw.B: Wakati wa usiku Paulo aliona maono: mtu mmoja wa Makedonia alikuwa amesimama akimsihi, "Vuka uje Makedonia utusaidie!"
sw.R: Usiku huo Mungu alimwonyesha Paulo maono. Ndani ya maono hayo, mtu mmoja wa Makedonia alikuwa amesimama akimsihi, "Vuka bahari uje Makedonia, utusaidie!"

decisions.choice: a vision: something seen that God sends
decisions.reason: Luke uses the word for the visions by which God guided Ananias (9:10), Cornelius (10:3), Peter (10:17) and Paul again at Corinth (18:9).

decisions.choice: Macedonia: the Roman province north of Greece, across the Aegean Sea
decisions.reason: Its cities included Philippi, Thessalonica and Beroea, where the next chapters go. The text does not say how Paul knew that the man was a Macedonian; his words make it plain.

decisions.choice: help us: the help is the gospel
alternatives: help in a war or a famine
decisions.reason: Paul and the others take the call as God's call to bring the gospel there (16:10).

decisions.choice: God showed Paul a vision
decisions.reason: Readable says who sent the vision, as the meaning note and 16:10 explain.

decisions.choice: come across the sea
decisions.reason: Readable says what lay between Troas and Macedonia.

source.text: ὡς δὲ τὸ ὅραμα εἶδεν, εὐθέως ἐζητήσαμεν ἐξελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν, συμβιβάζοντες ὅτι προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς ὁ θεὸς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: When then the vision he saw, immediately we sought to go forth into Macedonia, concluding that has called us the God to preach the gospel to them.

en.L: And when he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out into Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to preach the gospel to them.
en.B: As soon as he had seen the vision, we looked for a way to set out for Macedonia, sure now that God had called us to bring the gospel to its people.
en.R: After Paul saw the vision, we started at once to look for a way to get to Macedonia. We were sure that God was calling us to tell the people there the good news.

es.L: Y cuando vio la visión, enseguida procuramos salir hacia Macedonia, concluyendo que Dios nos había llamado a anunciarles la buena noticia.
es.B: Tan pronto como tuvo la visión, buscamos la manera de partir hacia Macedonia, convencidos ya de que Dios nos había llamado a anunciar la buena noticia a sus habitantes.
es.R: Después de que Pablo vio la visión, enseguida empezamos a buscar cómo llegar a Macedonia. Estábamos seguros de que Dios nos estaba llamando a contarle la buena noticia a la gente de allí.

sw.L: Na alipoyaona maono hayo, mara moja tulitafuta kwenda Makedonia, tukihitimisha kwamba Mungu ametuita tuwahubirie habari njema.
sw.B: Mara alipoyaona maono hayo, tulitafuta njia ya kwenda Makedonia, tukiwa na hakika sasa kwamba Mungu alikuwa ametuita tuwahubirie watu wa huko habari njema.
sw.R: Baada ya Paulo kuona maono hayo, mara moja tulianza kutafuta njia ya kwenda Makedonia. Tulikuwa na hakika kwamba Mungu alikuwa akituita tuwaambie watu wa huko habari njema.

decisions.choice: we: the narrator now counts himself among Paul's companions
alternatives: the narrator copies another person's diary
a style of storytelling with no real narrator present
decisions.reason: Up to here the story speaks of "they". From this sentence the narrator says "we", and he does so until the arrest at Philippi (16:17), and again from Philippi onward (20:5-21:18; 27:1-28:16). He was present for these events. The text never names him; who he was is a question for the book as a whole, and the translation does not settle it.

decisions.choice: concluding: reasoning it out together from the vision
decisions.reason: The verb means to put things together and draw a conclusion. The vision called; they understood it as God's call.

decisions.choice: to them: the people of Macedonia
alternatives: the man of the vision only
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers back to Macedonia, meaning those who live there.

decisions.choice: its people
decisions.reason: Balanced says whom the pronoun means, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: tell the good news
decisions.reason: Readable uses "good news" for the gospel, as everywhere.

decisions.choice: anunciar la buena noticia
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering of this verb, recorded once in this chapter. It says in plain words what is announced; "evangelizar" is a church word that many readers do not hear as "bring good news".

decisions.choice: kuhubiri habari njema (L, B); kuwaambia habari njema (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering of this verb, recorded once in this chapter. It says in plain words what is announced; "Injili" is kept for the gospel named as a message.

source.text: Ἀναχθέντες οὖν ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος εὐθυδρομήσαμεν εἰς Σαμοθρᾴκην, τῇ δὲ ἐπιούσῃ εἰς Νέαν Πόλιν, κἀκεῖθεν εἰς Φιλίππους, ἥτις ἐστὶν πρώτη τῆς μερίδος Μακεδονίας πόλις, κολωνία.

records.literal_gloss: Having set sail therefore from Troas we ran a straight course to Samothrace, the and following [day] to Nea Polis, \v 12 and from there to Philippi, which is a leading of the district of Macedonia city, a colony.

en.L: So setting sail from Troas, we ran a straight course to Samothrace, and on the next [day] to Neapolis, \v 12 and from there to Philippi, which is a leading city of the district of Macedonia, a colony.
en.B: So we set sail from Troas and ran with a straight course to Samothrace, and the next day reached Neapolis. \v 12 From there we made our way to Philippi, which ranks as a leading city of its district of Macedonia and is a Roman colony.
en.R: We sailed from Troas straight to the island of Samothrace. The next day we sailed on to the town of Neapolis. \v 12 From there we went to the city of Philippi. It was an important city in that part of Macedonia. It was also a Roman colony, a city that Rome had settled with its own citizens.

es.L: Así que, zarpando de Troas, navegamos en línea recta a Samotracia, y al [día] siguiente a Neápolis, \v 12 y de allí a Filipos, que es una ciudad principal del distrito de Macedonia, una colonia.
es.B: Así que zarpamos de Troas y navegamos directamente a Samotracia, y al día siguiente llegamos a Neápolis. \v 12 De allí fuimos a Filipos, una de las principales ciudades de aquel distrito de Macedonia y colonia romana.
es.R: Navegamos desde Troas directamente hasta la isla de Samotracia. Al día siguiente seguimos hasta el pueblo de Neápolis. \v 12 De allí fuimos a la ciudad de Filipos. Era una ciudad importante en esa parte de Macedonia. También era una colonia romana, una ciudad donde Roma había establecido a sus propios ciudadanos.

sw.L: Basi tukiisha kung'oa nanga kutoka Troa, tulisafiri moja kwa moja mpaka Samothrake, na [siku] iliyofuata mpaka Neapoli, \v 12 na kutoka huko mpaka Filipi, ulio mji wa kwanza wa wilaya ya Makedonia, koloni.
sw.B: Basi tuliondoka Troa kwa merikebu, tukasafiri moja kwa moja mpaka Samothrake, na siku iliyofuata tukafika Neapoli. \v 12 Kutoka huko tulikwenda Filipi, mji mmoja mashuhuri wa wilaya hiyo ya Makedonia, nao ni koloni la Kirumi.
sw.R: Tulisafiri kwa merikebu kutoka Troa moja kwa moja mpaka kisiwa cha Samothrake. Siku iliyofuata tukaendelea mpaka mji wa Neapoli. \v 12 Kutoka huko tulikwenda mpaka mji wa Filipi. Ulikuwa mji muhimu katika sehemu ile ya Makedonia. Pia ulikuwa koloni la Kirumi, yaani mji ambao Roma ilikuwa imeweka raia wake wenyewe waishi humo.

decisions.choice: ran a straight course: sailed straight there, with a good wind
decisions.reason: The verb is a sailor's word for a straight run. The voyage took two days; the same trip the other way took five (20:6).

decisions.choice: Samothrace, an island on the way; Neapolis, the port of Philippi
decisions.reason: Samothrace is a mountainous island in the north Aegean, a usual stop overnight. Neapolis is the modern Kavala, about ten miles from Philippi.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "a leading city of the district of Macedonia"
alternatives: "a city of the first district of Macedonia"
decisions.reason: The manuscripts differ in small ways at this point. The SBLGNT follows the reading of most early manuscripts. A reading that changes one letter, "of the first district", is supported by a few Latin manuscripts and is preferred by some editors, because Rome had divided Macedonia into four districts (Livy 45.29) and Philippi lay in the first. Codex Bezae calls Philippi the capital. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: leading: first in rank or importance, not the capital
decisions.reason: Amphipolis was the chief city of Philippi's district, and Thessalonica the capital of the province. Without the article, the word is best read as one of the foremost cities, a title cities used with pride.

decisions.choice: a colony: a Roman colony, a piece of Rome abroad
decisions.reason: After the battle of Philippi in 42 BC, and again after Actium in 31 BC, Rome settled veterans there. A colony was governed by Roman law, with its own Roman magistrates, and its citizens were Roman citizens. This explains the charge of 16:21 and Paul's protest in 16:37.

decisions.choice: the island of; the town of; the city of
decisions.reason: Readable says what each place was.

decisions.choice: Roman colony (B); a city that Rome had settled with its own citizens (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose colony it was, and Readable what that meant, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: Neapolis
decisions.reason: The two Greek words, meaning New City, are the town's name, written as one word.

decisions.choice: una ciudad principal (L); una de las principales ciudades (B); una ciudad importante (R)
decisions.reason: The word means first in rank or importance, not the capital and not the first city reached (meaning decision m4). "La primera ciudad" would suggest one of those; each level says "leading" in its own way.

decisions.choice: mji wa kwanza (L); mji mmoja mashuhuri (B); mji muhimu (R)
decisions.reason: The word means first in rank or importance, not the capital (meaning decision m4). "Mji mkuu" is the Swahili for a capital city, so it is avoided; Literal keeps "wa kwanza", which in Swahili can mean first in rank.

source.text: ἦμεν δὲ ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει διατρίβοντες ἡμέρας τινάς.

records.literal_gloss: We were then in this the city staying days some.

en.L: And we were staying in this city some days.
en.B: We spent several days in that city.
en.R: We stayed in Philippi for several days.

es.L: Y estuvimos en esta ciudad pasando algunos días.
es.B: Pasamos varios días en aquella ciudad.
es.R: Nos quedamos en Filipos varios días.

sw.L: Na tulikuwa katika mji huu tukikaa siku kadhaa.
sw.B: Tulikaa katika mji ule siku kadhaa.
sw.R: Tulikaa Filipi kwa siku kadhaa.

decisions.choice: were staying: a stay of some days before the Sabbath of 16:13
decisions.reason: The words are vague. The stay before the first Sabbath was short; the whole stay was longer (16:18).

decisions.choice: Philippi
decisions.reason: Readable names the city.

source.text: τῇ τε ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ἐξήλθομεν ἔξω τῆς πύλης παρὰ ποταμὸν οὗ ἐνομίζομεν προσευχὴν εἶναι, καὶ καθίσαντες ἐλαλοῦμεν ταῖς συνελθούσαις γυναιξίν.

records.literal_gloss: On the and day of the Sabbaths we went forth outside the gate beside a river where we were supposing a place of prayer to be, and having sat down we were speaking to the having come together women.

en.L: And on the Sabbath day we went out outside the gate beside a river, where we supposed there was a place of prayer, and sitting down, we were speaking to the women who had come together.
en.B: On the Sabbath day we went out beyond the gate, beside a river, where we thought there might be a place of prayer. We took a seat and spoke to the women who had come together.
en.R: On the Sabbath day we went out of the city gate to the river. We thought Jewish people might meet there to pray. We sat down and talked to the women who had come there.

es.L: Y el día sábado salimos fuera de la puerta, junto a un río, donde suponíamos que había un lugar de oración; y sentándonos, hablábamos a las mujeres que se habían reunido.
es.B: El sábado salimos más allá de la puerta, junto a un río, donde pensábamos que habría un lugar de oración. Nos sentamos y hablamos a las mujeres que se habían reunido.
es.R: El sábado salimos por la puerta de la ciudad y fuimos al río. Pensábamos que tal vez allí se reunían judíos para orar. Nos sentamos y hablamos con las mujeres que habían llegado.

sw.L: Na siku ya Sabato tulitoka nje ya lango kando ya mto, ambapo tulidhani kuna mahali pa maombi; na tukiketi, tulikuwa tukizungumza na wanawake waliokusanyika.
sw.B: Siku ya Sabato tulitoka nje ya lango, tukaenda kando ya mto, ambapo tulidhani pangekuwa na mahali pa maombi. Tukaketi, tukazungumza na wanawake waliokuwa wamekusanyika huko.
sw.R: Siku ya Sabato tulitoka nje ya lango la mji, tukaenda mtoni. Tulidhani labda Wayahudi walikutana huko kuomba. Tukaketi, tukazungumza na wanawake waliokuwa wamefika pale.

decisions.choice: a place of prayer: a place where Jews met for prayer
decisions.reason: The word means prayer, and was used for a Jewish meeting place, often a building (Josephus, and inscriptions from Egypt). Here it may be an open place by the water. No synagogue is named at Philippi, perhaps because few Jews lived there; only women are mentioned.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "where we supposed there was a place of prayer"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ between a form meaning "we supposed" and one meaning "it was customary". The SBLGNT reads the first. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the day of the Sabbaths: the Sabbath day
decisions.reason: The plural is a usual way of naming the Sabbath (Luke 4:16).

decisions.choice: sitting down: the posture of a teacher
decisions.reason: Teachers sat to teach in the synagogue (Luke 4:20).

decisions.choice: Jewish people might meet there to pray
alternatives: there was a place of prayer
decisions.reason: Readable says what a place of prayer was, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: καί τις γυνὴ ὀνόματι Λυδία, πορφυρόπωλις πόλεως Θυατείρων σεβομένη τὸν θεόν, ἤκουεν, ἧς ὁ κύριος διήνοιξεν τὴν καρδίαν προσέχειν τοῖς λαλουμένοις ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου.

records.literal_gloss: And a certain woman by name Lydia, a seller of purple of a city of Thyatira, worshiping the God, was listening, of whom the Lord opened the heart to pay attention to the things being spoken by the Paul.

en.L: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple [cloth] from the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God, was listening; the Lord opened her heart to pay attention to the things spoken by Paul.
en.B: A woman named Lydia was listening, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who worshiped God. The Lord opened her heart to heed what Paul was saying.
en.R: A woman named Lydia was there listening. She was from the city of Thyatira, and she sold costly purple cloth. She was not a Jew, but she worshiped the God of Israel. The Lord opened her heart, so that she paid close attention to what Paul said.

es.L: Y una mujer llamada Lidia, vendedora de púrpura de la ciudad de Tiatira, que adoraba a Dios, escuchaba; el Señor le abrió el corazón para que atendiera a lo que Pablo decía.
es.B: Escuchaba también una mujer llamada Lidia, comerciante en telas de púrpura, de la ciudad de Tiatira, que adoraba a Dios. El Señor le abrió el corazón para que acogiera lo que Pablo decía.
es.R: Una mujer llamada Lidia estaba allí escuchando. Era de la ciudad de Tiatira y vendía telas de púrpura, que eran muy caras. No era judía, pero adoraba al Dios de Israel. El Señor le abrió el corazón, y ella prestó mucha atención a lo que Pablo decía.

sw.L: Na mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Lidia, mwuzaji wa [nguo za] zambarau wa mji wa Thiatira, aliyekuwa akimwabudu Mungu, alikuwa akisikiliza; Bwana akaufungua moyo wake ayatilie maanani yaliyokuwa yakisemwa na Paulo.
sw.B: Mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Lidia alikuwa akisikiliza; alikuwa mfanyabiashara wa nguo za zambarau kutoka mji wa Thiatira, naye alimwabudu Mungu. Bwana aliufungua moyo wake ayatilie maanani maneno ya Paulo.
sw.R: Mwanamke mmoja aitwaye Lidia alikuwa pale akisikiliza. Alitoka mji wa Thiatira, na aliuza nguo za zambarau zenye bei kubwa. Hakuwa Myahudi, lakini alimwabudu Mungu wa Israeli. Bwana aliufungua moyo wake, akasikiliza kwa makini yale aliyosema Paulo.

decisions.choice: a seller of purple: a trader in cloth dyed purple
decisions.reason: Purple dye was costly, and purple cloth was worn by the wealthy. Thyatira, in the region of Lydia in Asia, was known for its dyers, as inscriptions from the city show. A trader in such goods was likely a woman of some means; she has a house large enough for guests (16:15).

decisions.choice: who worshiped God: a Gentile who worshiped the God of Israel
decisions.reason: Luke uses this phrase and "those who fear God" for Gentiles who joined in Jewish worship without becoming Jews, like Cornelius (10:2) and some in Thessalonica and Corinth (17:4, 18:7). She was with the Jewish women at prayer.

decisions.choice: the Lord opened her heart: God's work brought her to faith
decisions.reason: The risen Jesus opened the minds of the disciples to understand the Scriptures (Luke 24:45). The heart stands for mind and will. Her listening was real, and the Lord made it fruitful. "The Lord" may be Jesus or God; Luke often leaves it open.

decisions.choice: pay attention to: take to heart and respond
decisions.reason: The verb means to give heed to something, and act on it, as in 8:6.

decisions.choice: she was not a Jew, but she worshiped the God of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase implied, as the meaning note explains. It is not certain that she was not Jewish.

decisions.choice: costly
decisions.reason: Readable says why purple cloth mattered.

decisions.choice: aliyekuwa akimwabudu Mungu (L); alimwabudu Mungu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says she worshiped God, and the meaning is a Gentile who worshiped the God of Israel (meaning decision m2). "Mcha Mungu" would be heard as "a devout person" in general; Readable says she was not a Jew, as the English does.

source.text: ὡς δὲ ἐβαπτίσθη καὶ ὁ οἶκος αὐτῆς, παρεκάλεσεν λέγουσα· Εἰ κεκρίκατέ με πιστὴν τῷ κυρίῳ εἶναι, εἰσελθόντες εἰς τὸν οἶκόν μου μένετε· καὶ παρεβιάσατο ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: When then she was baptized and the household of her, she urged saying, If you have judged me faithful to the Lord to be, having come into the house of me stay; and she prevailed upon us.

en.L: And when she and her household were baptized, she urged [us], saying, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house [and] stay." And she prevailed upon us.
en.B: After she and her household had been baptized, she pressed us to accept her offer: "If you are satisfied that I am faithful to the Lord, come into my home and stay." And she would not take no for an answer.
en.R: Lydia and the people in her home were baptized. Then she begged us, "If you agree that I truly trust in the Lord, come and stay in my house." She kept asking until we agreed.

es.L: Y cuando fue bautizada, y también su casa, [nos] rogó diciendo: «Si {{plural_you:han juzgado|habéis juzgado}} que yo soy fiel al Señor, {{plural_you:entren|entrad}} en mi casa [y] {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}}». Y nos obligó [a aceptar].
es.B: Después de ser bautizada junto con los de su casa, nos insistió: «Si {{plural_you:consideran|consideráis}} que soy fiel al Señor, {{plural_you:vengan|venid}} a mi casa y {{plural_you:quédense|quedaos}} en ella». Y no nos dejó decir que no.
es.R: Lidia y los de su casa fueron bautizados. Después nos rogó: «Si {{plural_you:están|estáis}} de acuerdo en que de verdad confío en el Señor, {{plural_you:vengan a quedarse|venid a quedaros}} en mi casa». Insistió hasta que aceptamos.

sw.L: Na alipobatizwa, yeye na nyumba yake, alitusihi akisema, "Ikiwa mmeamua kuwa mimi ni mwaminifu kwa Bwana, ingieni nyumbani mwangu mkae." Akatushurutisha.
sw.B: Alipokwisha kubatizwa pamoja na watu wa nyumbani mwake, alitusihi, akisema, "Ikiwa mmeridhika kwamba mimi ni mwaminifu kwa Bwana, njooni nyumbani kwangu mkae." Hakukubali tukatae.
sw.R: Lidia na watu wa nyumbani mwake walibatizwa. Kisha akatusihi, "Ikiwa mnakubali kwamba kweli ninamwamini Bwana, njooni mkae nyumbani kwangu." Aliendelea kutusihi mpaka tukakubali.

decisions.choice: her household: those who lived under her roof, family and servants
decisions.reason: A household took in relatives, slaves and others who lived in the house. No husband is named, so she seems to have been its head. The text does not say whether there were children, or how old they were.

decisions.choice: faithful to the Lord: a true believer in the Lord
decisions.reason: The word can mean believing or trustworthy. Here it is the result of her baptism: she asks them to accept that she truly belongs to the Lord.

decisions.choice: prevailed upon: urged them until they gave in
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of the two disciples urging Jesus to stay at Emmaus (Luke 24:29).

decisions.choice: she would not take no for an answer
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the verb's sense of pressing until the other side yields into everyday words.

decisions.choice: truly trust in
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense chosen in the meaning note.

source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ πορευομένων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν παιδίσκην τινὰ ἔχουσαν πνεῦμα πύθωνα ὑπαντῆσαι ἡμῖν, ἥτις ἐργασίαν πολλὴν παρεῖχεν τοῖς κυρίοις αὐτῆς μαντευομένη·

records.literal_gloss: It happened then, going of us to the place of prayer, a slave girl certain having a spirit, a python, met us, who profit much was bringing to the masters of her by fortune-telling.

en.L: And it happened, as we were going to the place of prayer, [that] a certain slave girl having a spirit of Python met us, who brought her masters much profit by fortune-telling.
en.B: Once, on our way to the place of prayer, a slave girl came to meet us who had a soothsaying spirit. Her fortune-telling brought in a large income for her masters.
en.R: One day we were going to the place of prayer. A slave girl met us who had a spirit in her that let her tell people what would happen in the future. Her owners made a lot of money from her fortune-telling.

es.L: Y sucedió que, yendo nosotros al lugar de oración, nos salió al encuentro una joven esclava que tenía un espíritu de Pitón, la cual daba mucha ganancia a sus amos adivinando.
es.B: Un día, cuando íbamos al lugar de oración, nos salió al encuentro una joven esclava que tenía un espíritu de adivinación. Con sus adivinaciones daba grandes ganancias a sus amos.
es.R: Un día íbamos al lugar de oración. Nos salió al encuentro una joven esclava que tenía dentro un espíritu que le permitía decirle a la gente lo que iba a pasar en el futuro. Sus dueños ganaban mucho dinero con lo que ella adivinaba.

sw.L: Na ikawa, tulipokuwa tukienda mahali pa maombi, kijakazi mmoja mwenye pepo wa Pithoni alikutana nasi, ambaye aliwaletea mabwana zake faida nyingi kwa kubashiri.
sw.B: Siku moja, tulipokuwa tukienda mahali pa maombi, msichana mmoja mtumwa alikutana nasi. Alikuwa na pepo wa uaguzi, na kwa kubashiri aliwapatia mabwana zake mapato makubwa.
sw.R: Siku moja tulikuwa tukienda mahali pa maombi. Msichana mmoja mtumwa alikutana nasi. Alikuwa na pepo ndani yake aliyemwezesha kuwaambia watu mambo yatakayotokea baadaye. Wamiliki wake walipata pesa nyingi kutokana na ubashiri wake.

decisions.choice: a spirit of Python: a spirit that gave oracles, as people believed the god of Delphi did
decisions.reason: Python was the serpent of Greek myth that guarded Delphi, the most famous oracle of the Greek world, before Apollo killed it. The name came to be used for a spirit that spoke through someone to foretell things, and for the people it spoke through; Plutarch uses it of those who spoke in a trance. People in Philippi would have taken the girl to be inspired by Apollo.

decisions.choice: a spirit: a real spirit, which Paul drives out
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to the spirit and it comes out (16:18), as unclean spirits do at Jesus's command (Luke 4:33-35). Luke does not call it unclean, but he treats it as opposed to God's work.

decisions.choice: fortune-telling: pagan divination
decisions.reason: This verb is used in the Greek Old Testament for the divination God forbids (Deuteronomy 18:10; 1 Samuel 28:8), never for the prophets of the Lord.

decisions.choice: a slave girl and her masters: she was owned, perhaps by partners
decisions.reason: Her owners, more than one, profited from her powers, as owners of a skilled slave would.

decisions.choice: a soothsaying spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the name meant to its hearers; Literal keeps the name, which the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: a spirit in her that let her tell people what would happen in the future
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the spirit did.

decisions.choice: slave girl
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it for people owned as property: her owners made money from her (m4).

decisions.choice: una joven esclava (every level)
decisions.reason: The term sheet gives "criada" for this word, but here she is owned and her masters live off her (meaning decision m4), and the English says "slave girl" at every level, so Spanish names her as a slave too.

decisions.choice: un espíritu de Pitón (L); un espíritu de adivinación (B); un espíritu que le permitía decir lo que iba a pasar (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the name, which points to the oracle of Delphi (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say what the spirit did, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kijakazi (L); msichana mtumwa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet gives "mtumishi wa kike" at Balanced and Readable, but here slavery itself is the point: she is owned and her masters live off her (meaning decision m4). So Balanced and Readable say "mtumwa", as the term sheet allows where slavery is meant.

decisions.choice: pepo wa Pithoni (L); pepo wa uaguzi (B); pepo aliyemwezesha kuwaambia watu mambo yatakayotokea (R)
decisions.reason: "Pepo", the term-sheet word for an evil spirit, since Paul drives it out (meaning decision m2); "roho" is kept for the Holy Spirit and the human spirit. Literal keeps the name, which points to the oracle of Delphi (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say what the spirit did.

source.text: αὕτη κατακολουθοῦσα τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἡμῖν ἔκραζεν λέγουσα· Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι δοῦλοι τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου εἰσίν, οἵτινες καταγγέλλουσιν ὑμῖν ὁδὸν σωτηρίας.

records.literal_gloss: She following the Paul and us was crying out saying, These the men slaves of the God the Most High are, who proclaim to you a way of salvation.

en.L: She, following Paul and us, kept crying out, saying, "These men are slaves of the Most High God, who proclaim to you a way of salvation."
en.B: She trailed after Paul and the rest of us, crying out, "These men are servants of the Most High God, and they are announcing to you a way of salvation!"
en.R: She followed Paul and the rest of us around and kept shouting, "These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how you can be saved!"

es.L: Esta, siguiendo a Pablo y a nosotros, gritaba diciendo: «Estos hombres son esclavos del Dios Altísimo, los cuales {{plural_you:les|os}} anuncian un camino de salvación».
es.B: Ella iba detrás de Pablo y de los demás, y gritaba: «¡Estos hombres son siervos del Dios Altísimo, y {{plural_you:les|os}} anuncian un camino de salvación!».
es.R: Seguía a Pablo y a los demás por todas partes, y gritaba una y otra vez: «¡Estos hombres son siervos del Dios Altísimo! ¡Ellos {{plural_you:les|os}} dicen cómo {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} ser salvos!».

sw.L: Huyo, akimfuata Paulo na sisi, alikuwa akipiga kelele akisema, "Watu hawa ni watumwa wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, ambao wanawatangazia njia ya wokovu."
sw.B: Alikuwa akimfuata Paulo na sisi wengine, akipaza sauti, "Watu hawa ni watumishi wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, nao wanawatangazia njia ya wokovu!"
sw.R: Alimfuata Paulo na sisi wengine kila mahali, akipiga kelele tena na tena, "Watu hawa ni watumishi wa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa! Wanawaambia jinsi mnavyoweza kuokolewa!"

decisions.choice: the Most High God: true in itself, but a title pagans also used for their highest god
decisions.reason: The title goes back to Genesis 14:18-20. Demons cried out to Jesus as "Son of the Most High God" (Luke 8:28). In the Greek world, inscriptions honor Zeus and other gods as "the Most High", so hearers in Philippi might not have known which god was meant.

decisions.choice: a way of salvation: one way among others, as her hearers would take it
decisions.reason: There is no article. Her words are true as far as they go, but in a city of many gods they could sound like one more path. This may be why Paul was troubled (16:18).

decisions.choice: slaves: men wholly owned by God
decisions.reason: The word means a slave. The apostles use it of themselves (Romans 1:1; Philippians 1:1) and of believers in prayer (4:29).

decisions.choice: these men: Paul and his companions
decisions.reason: The word here points to particular men, the missionaries.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to you"
decisions.reason: The two Greek pronouns sounded alike and were often confused by copyists. "To you" is better attested. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: how you can be saved
decisions.reason: Readable puts the noun as a verb. It keeps the sense of the meaning note, since "how" does not claim it is the only way.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering, recorded once in this chapter, as the English: Literal shows that they are wholly owned by God (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say "siervos", since slavery itself is not the point here.

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering, recorded once in this chapter, as the English: Literal shows that they are wholly owned by God (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable say "watumishi", since slavery itself is not the point here.

source.text: τοῦτο δὲ ἐποίει ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας.

records.literal_gloss: This then she was doing for many days.

en.L: And she was doing this for many days.
en.B: She kept this up for many days.
en.R: She did this day after day for a long time.

es.L: Y esto hacía durante muchos días.
es.B: Así lo estuvo haciendo durante muchos días.
es.R: Hizo esto día tras día durante mucho tiempo.

sw.L: Na alikuwa akifanya hivyo siku nyingi.
sw.B: Aliendelea kufanya hivyo kwa siku nyingi.
sw.R: Alifanya hivyo siku baada ya siku kwa muda mrefu.

decisions.choice: was doing: again and again
decisions.reason: The imperfect shows that it went on day after day.

source.text: διαπονηθεὶς δὲ Παῦλος καὶ ἐπιστρέψας τῷ πνεύματι εἶπεν· Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς· καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Having been greatly troubled then Paul and having turned to the spirit said, I command you in name of Jesus Christ to come out from her; and it came out in the same hour.

en.L: But Paul, greatly troubled, turned and said to the spirit, "I command you in [the] name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to come out of her." And it came out that very hour.
en.B: In the end Paul grew weary and vexed. He turned and told the spirit, "I order you in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} to come out of her!" It came out that same hour.
en.R: Paul became very upset. He turned around and said to the spirit, "By the power of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, I order you to come out of her!" At once the spirit left her.

es.L: Pero Pablo, muy molesto, se volvió y dijo al espíritu: «Te ordeno en [el] nombre de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}} que salgas de ella». Y salió en aquella misma hora.
es.B: Al final Pablo, cansado y molesto, se volvió y le dijo al espíritu: «¡En el nombre de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, te ordeno que salgas de ella!». Y en ese mismo momento salió.
es.R: Pablo se molestó mucho. Se dio vuelta y le dijo al espíritu: «¡Por el poder de {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, te ordeno que salgas de ella!». Al instante el espíritu salió de ella.

sw.L: Lakini Paulo, akiwa amechukizwa sana, aligeuka akamwambia yule pepo, "Nakuamuru kwa jina la Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} umtoke." Naye akamtoka saa ile ile.
sw.B: Mwishowe Paulo alichoshwa na kuudhika, akageuka, akamwambia yule pepo, "Nakuamuru kwa jina la Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}: mtoke msichana huyu!" Pepo huyo akamtoka saa ile ile.
sw.R: Paulo aliudhika sana. Akageuka, akamwambia yule pepo, "Kwa uwezo wa Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, nakuamuru umtoke msichana huyu!" Mara moja yule pepo akamtoka.

decisions.choice: greatly troubled: annoyed and worn down
decisions.reason: The verb means to be deeply disturbed or exasperated; the leaders were so with the apostles in 4:2. Luke does not say why: perhaps the noise, perhaps that a pagan spirit was announcing the message and confusing it.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus Christ: by his authority and power
decisions.reason: As in 3:6 and 3:16, the name stands for the person. In 19:13-16 those who use the name like a spell are overpowered.

decisions.choice: that very hour: at once
decisions.reason: An hour often means simply the moment (Luke 2:38, 7:21).

decisions.choice: by the power of
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name means here, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: in the end
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that his patience ran out after many days (16:18).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}
decisions.reason: The English span covers only "Christ". Spanish writes the name as one word, "Jesucristo", so the span takes in the whole name, as the term sheet sets for every "Jesus Christ".

source.text: Ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ κύριοι αὐτῆς ὅτι ἐξῆλθεν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας αὐτῶν ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας, καὶ προσαγαγόντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς στρατηγοῖς εἶπαν· Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐκταράσσουσιν ἡμῶν τὴν πόλιν Ἰουδαῖοι ὑπάρχοντες, καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν Ῥωμαίοις οὖσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the masters of her that went out the hope of the profit of them, having seized the Paul and the Silas they dragged [them] into the marketplace before the rulers, \v 20 and having brought them to the magistrates they said, These the men are throwing into confusion our the city, Jews being, \v 21 and they proclaim customs which not it is lawful for us to accept nor to practice, Romans being.

en.L: But when her masters saw that the hope of their profit had gone out, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged [them] into the marketplace before the rulers, \v 20 and bringing them to the magistrates, they said, "These men are throwing our city into confusion, being Jews, \v 21 and they proclaim customs that it is not lawful for us to accept or to practice, being Romans."
en.B: Her masters saw that their hope of gain had gone out of her along with the spirit. So they laid hold of Paul and Silas and hauled them off to the rulers in the marketplace. \v 20 Bringing them before the magistrates, they said, "These men are upsetting our whole city. They are Jews, \v 21 and they preach customs that we cannot lawfully take up or follow, since we are Romans."
en.R: The girl's owners saw that she could no longer make money for them. So they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them to the city leaders in the marketplace. \v 20 They brought them to the chief officials of the city and said, "These men are Jews, and they are causing a lot of trouble in our city. \v 21 They are teaching customs that we Romans are not allowed to accept or follow."

es.L: Pero al ver sus amos que había salido la esperanza de su ganancia, prendieron a Pablo y a Silas y [los] arrastraron a la plaza ante las autoridades, \v 20 y presentándolos a los magistrados, dijeron: «Estos hombres están alborotando nuestra ciudad, siendo judíos, \v 21 y anuncian costumbres que no nos es lícito aceptar ni practicar, siendo romanos».
es.B: Cuando sus amos vieron que, con el espíritu, había salido de ella también su esperanza de ganancia, agarraron a Pablo y a Silas y los arrastraron ante las autoridades en la plaza pública. \v 20 Los presentaron ante los magistrados y dijeron: «Estos hombres están alborotando toda nuestra ciudad. Son judíos, \v 21 y enseñan costumbres que a nosotros, como romanos, no nos está permitido adoptar ni practicar».
es.R: Los dueños de la muchacha vieron que ella ya no podía ganar dinero para ellos. Entonces agarraron a Pablo y a Silas y los llevaron a rastras ante los jefes de la ciudad, en la plaza. \v 20 Los llevaron ante los principales funcionarios de la ciudad y dijeron: «Estos hombres son judíos, y están causando muchos problemas en nuestra ciudad. \v 21 Enseñan costumbres que nosotros, los romanos, no podemos aceptar ni seguir».

sw.L: Lakini mabwana zake walipoona kwamba tumaini la faida yao limetoka, waliwakamata Paulo na Sila, wakawaburuta mpaka sokoni mbele ya watawala, \v 20 na wakiisha kuwaleta kwa mahakimu, walisema, "Watu hawa wanauvuruga mji wetu, wakiwa Wayahudi, \v 21 nao wanatangaza desturi ambazo si halali kwetu kuzipokea wala kuzifanya, tukiwa Warumi."
sw.B: Mabwana zake walipoona kwamba tumaini lao la kupata faida limetoka pamoja na yule pepo, waliwakamata Paulo na Sila, wakawaburuta mpaka kwa watawala kwenye uwanja wa soko. \v 20 Wakawaleta mbele ya mahakimu, wakasema, "Watu hawa wanauvuruga mji wetu wote. Wao ni Wayahudi, \v 21 nao wanafundisha desturi ambazo sisi, kwa kuwa ni Warumi, haturuhusiwi kisheria kuzikubali wala kuzifuata."
sw.R: Wamiliki wa yule msichana waliona kwamba hangeweza tena kuwapatia pesa. Basi wakawakamata Paulo na Sila, wakawaburuta mpaka kwa viongozi wa mji sokoni. \v 20 Wakawaleta mbele ya maafisa wakuu wa mji, wakasema, "Watu hawa ni Wayahudi, nao wanaleta fujo kubwa katika mji wetu. \v 21 Wanafundisha desturi ambazo sisi Warumi hatuna ruhusa kuzikubali wala kuzifuata."

decisions.choice: gone out: the same verb as for the spirit coming out
decisions.reason: The spirit "came out" (16:18) and the owners' hope of profit "went out" with it. The repeated verb makes a grim joke.

decisions.choice: rulers and magistrates: the same men, the chief officials of the colony
decisions.reason: "Rulers" is a general word for those in authority. "Magistrates" renders the Greek word for generals, which was used in Greek cities for the two chief officials who ran a Roman colony, known in Latin as duumvirs or praetors. Luke uses the word only of these officials from here on (16:22, 35, 36, 38).

decisions.choice: the marketplace: the forum, the city's public square
decisions.reason: The forum held the courts and offices of the city's officials. The foundations of the forum of Roman Philippi can still be seen.

decisions.choice: being Jews: an appeal to feeling against Jews
decisions.reason: The owners say nothing of their lost income. They set "Jews" against "Romans" (16:21). About this time the emperor Claudius ordered Jews out of Rome (18:2).

decisions.choice: customs not lawful for Romans: foreign religious ways that Romans should not take up
decisions.reason: Romans held that citizens should not adopt foreign cults that were not approved. The charge is vague, but it was serious in a colony that prided itself on being Roman.

decisions.choice: out of her along with the spirit
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wordplay of the meaning note by saying what went out with what.

decisions.choice: the chief officials of the city
decisions.reason: Readable describes the office instead of naming it, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: she could no longer make money for them
alternatives: the hope of their profit had gone out
decisions.reason: Readable says what the loss was; the wordplay cannot be kept in plain words.

decisions.choice: las autoridades, los magistrados (L, B); los jefes de la ciudad, los principales funcionarios de la ciudad (R)
decisions.reason: Two words for the same chief officials of the colony (meaning decision m2). "Magistrados" is used for the second word through the rest of the chapter; "pretores", the Latin title, would need explaining. Readable says who they were, as the English does.

decisions.choice: watawala, mahakimu (L, B); viongozi wa mji, maafisa wakuu wa mji (R)
decisions.reason: Two words for the same chief officials of the colony (meaning decision m2). "Mahakimu" (magistrates) is used for the second word through the rest of the chapter, since these men also sat in judgment; Readable says who they were, as the English does.

decisions.choice: limetoka (L, B), as the spirit "akamtoka" (verse 18)
decisions.reason: Luke uses the same verb for the hope of profit going out as for the spirit coming out (meaning decision m1). Literal and Balanced keep "kutoka" so the play on words can still be heard; Readable says what it meant.

source.text: καὶ συνεπέστη ὁ ὄχλος κατ’ αὐτῶν, καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐκέλευον ῥαβδίζειν, πολλάς τε ἐπιθέντες αὐτοῖς πληγὰς ἔβαλον εἰς φυλακήν, παραγγείλαντες τῷ δεσμοφύλακι ἀσφαλῶς τηρεῖν αὐτούς·

records.literal_gloss: And rose up together the crowd against them, and the magistrates having torn off of them the garments were ordering to beat with rods, \v 23 many and having laid on them blows they threw [them] into prison, having commanded the jailer securely to keep them;

en.L: And the crowd rose up together against them, and the magistrates, tearing off their garments, ordered [them] to be beaten with rods, \v 23 and after laying many blows on them, they threw [them] into prison, commanding the jailer to guard them securely.
en.B: The crowd too rose up against them, and the magistrates tore the clothes off them and ordered them beaten with rods. \v 23 When they had struck them many blows, they threw them into prison and told the jailer to keep them safely locked up.
en.R: A crowd of people joined in and turned against Paul and Silas. The city officials had their clothes torn off and ordered men to beat them with wooden rods. \v 23 They beat Paul and Silas many times. Then they threw them into prison and told the jailer to keep them locked up tight.

es.L: Y la multitud se levantó a una contra ellos, y los magistrados, rasgándoles las ropas, ordenaban que [los] azotaran con varas, \v 23 y después de darles muchos golpes, [los] echaron en la cárcel, mandando al carcelero que los guardara con seguridad.
es.B: También la multitud se levantó contra ellos, y los magistrados les arrancaron la ropa y ordenaron azotarlos con varas. \v 23 Después de darles muchos golpes, los echaron en la cárcel y ordenaron al carcelero que los vigilara con todo cuidado.
es.R: Mucha gente se unió y se puso en contra de Pablo y Silas. Los funcionarios de la ciudad mandaron que les quitaran la ropa y ordenaron a unos hombres que los golpearan con varas de madera. \v 23 Golpearon a Pablo y a Silas muchas veces. Luego los echaron en la cárcel y le dijeron al carcelero que los tuviera bien encerrados.

sw.L: Na umati ukainuka pamoja dhidi yao, na mahakimu, wakiwararulia mavazi yao, waliamuru wapigwe kwa fimbo, \v 23 na baada ya kuwapiga mapigo mengi, waliwatupa gerezani, wakimwagiza mlinzi wa gereza awalinde kwa uthabiti.
sw.B: Umati wa watu nao uliinuka dhidi yao, na mahakimu wakawararulia nguo zao, wakaamuru wachapwe kwa fimbo. \v 23 Baada ya kuwachapa mapigo mengi, waliwatupa gerezani, wakamwagiza mlinzi wa gereza awalinde kwa uangalifu wasitoroke.
sw.R: Watu wengi pia walijiunga, wakawageukia Paulo na Sila. Maafisa wa mji waliamuru nguo zao zivuliwe, wakaamuru watu wawapige kwa fimbo za mti. \v 23 Waliwapiga Paulo na Sila mara nyingi. Kisha wakawatupa gerezani, wakamwambia mlinzi wa gereza awafungie ndani kwa uangalifu mkubwa.

decisions.choice: tearing off their garments: stripping Paul and Silas for the beating
alternatives: the magistrates tearing their own robes in outrage
decisions.reason: The pronoun could refer to the magistrates, but a Roman beating was given on the bare back, and the magistrates order it at once. The officials gave the order; their attendants did the stripping.

decisions.choice: beaten with rods: the Roman punishment carried out by the magistrates' attendants
decisions.reason: The attendants of Roman magistrates, the lictors, carried bundles of rods (16:35). Paul says he was beaten with rods three times (2 Corinthians 11:25) and speaks of being shamefully treated at Philippi (1 Thessalonians 2:2).

decisions.choice: guard them securely: keep them so they could not escape
decisions.reason: The adverb means safely or surely; the next verse shows what the jailer did to make sure.

decisions.choice: ordered men to beat them with wooden rods
alternatives: ordered them to be beaten with rods
decisions.reason: Readable says that others carried out the beating, and what the rods were.

decisions.choice: las ropas (L); la ropa (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps "manto" for the outer cloak, but here the word means their clothes in general, stripped off for the beating (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: mlinzi wa gereza (every level, through the chapter)
decisions.reason: The word means the man who kept the prisoners. "Mkuu wa gereza" would make him the head of a modern prison service; "mlinzi wa gereza" says plainly what he did.

source.text: ὃς παραγγελίαν τοιαύτην λαβὼν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ τοὺς πόδας ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ ξύλον.

records.literal_gloss: who an order such having received threw them into the inner prison and the feet fastened of them in the wood.

en.L: Having received such an order, he threw them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
en.B: Given such a charge, the jailer threw them into the inner part of the prison and made their feet fast in the stocks.
en.R: Because of this order, the jailer put them in a room deep inside the prison. He locked their feet between heavy blocks of wood so they could not move.

es.L: El cual, habiendo recibido tal orden, los echó en la cárcel de más adentro y les sujetó los pies en el cepo.
es.B: Al recibir esa orden, el carcelero los metió en la parte más interior de la cárcel y les aseguró los pies en el cepo.
es.R: Por esa orden, el carcelero los puso en un cuarto muy adentro de la cárcel. Les encerró los pies entre unos bloques pesados de madera para que no pudieran moverse.

sw.L: Naye, akiisha kupokea agizo kama hilo, aliwatupa katika gereza la ndani, akaifunga miguu yao katika mkatale.
sw.B: Mlinzi wa gereza alipopewa agizo hilo, aliwatia katika chumba cha ndani kabisa cha gereza, akaifunga miguu yao kwa mkatale.
sw.R: Kwa sababu ya agizo hilo, mlinzi wa gereza aliwaweka katika chumba kilichokuwa ndani kabisa ya gereza. Akaifungia miguu yao kati ya vipande vizito vya mti ili wasiweze kusogea.

decisions.choice: the stocks: a wooden frame that held the feet fast
decisions.reason: The word means wood. Stocks had holes for the legs and could be set to spread them painfully apart. With their backs torn from the beating, the prisoners could neither move nor lie easily.

decisions.choice: the inner prison: the innermost, most secure cell
decisions.reason: The jailer chose the place hardest to escape from, as ordered (16:23).

decisions.choice: between heavy blocks of wood so they could not move
decisions.reason: Readable describes the stocks.

decisions.choice: the jailer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject; the Greek joins this to the last sentence with "who".

source.text: Κατὰ δὲ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν θεόν, ἐπηκροῶντο δὲ αὐτῶν οἱ δέσμιοι·

records.literal_gloss: About then the midnight Paul and Silas praying were singing hymns to the God, were listening and to them the prisoners.

en.L: And about midnight Paul and Silas, praying, were singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.
en.B: At midnight, as Paul and Silas prayed, they sang praises to God, and the prisoners listened.
en.R: Around midnight Paul and Silas prayed and sang songs to praise God. The other prisoners in the jail heard them.

es.L: Y como a medianoche, Pablo y Silas, orando, cantaban himnos a Dios, y los presos los escuchaban.
es.B: A medianoche, mientras oraban, Pablo y Silas cantaban alabanzas a Dios, y los presos los escuchaban.
es.R: Cerca de la medianoche, Pablo y Silas oraban y cantaban canciones para alabar a Dios. Los otros presos de la cárcel los oían.

sw.L: Na yapata usiku wa manane Paulo na Sila, wakiomba, walikuwa wakimwimbia Mungu nyimbo za sifa, na wafungwa walikuwa wakiwasikiliza.
sw.B: Usiku wa manane, Paulo na Sila walipokuwa wakiomba, walimwimbia Mungu nyimbo za sifa, na wafungwa walikuwa wakiwasikiliza.
sw.R: Karibu na usiku wa manane Paulo na Sila waliomba na kuimba nyimbo za kumsifu Mungu. Wafungwa wengine gerezani waliwasikia.

decisions.choice: praying, singing hymns: prayer that took the form of song
decisions.reason: The participle and the verb go together: their prayer was sung praise, as in many Psalms.

decisions.choice: singing hymns: singing praise to God
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Jesus and the disciples singing after the last supper (Mark 14:26), probably Psalms.

decisions.choice: were listening: listening closely
decisions.reason: The verb means to listen attentively, as to a performance.

decisions.choice: the other prisoners in the jail
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that these were the others held there.

source.text: ἄφνω δὲ σεισμὸς ἐγένετο μέγας ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου, ἠνεῴχθησαν δὲ παραχρῆμα αἱ θύραι πᾶσαι, καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη.

records.literal_gloss: Suddenly then earthquake happened great so that were shaken the foundations of the prison; were opened then immediately the doors all, and of all the chains were unfastened.

en.L: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened, and the chains of all were unfastened.
en.B: All at once a great earthquake struck, so strong that the prison was shaken to its foundations. In that instant all the doors came open, and the chains of every prisoner fell loose.
en.R: Suddenly there was a strong earthquake. It shook the prison down to its foundations. Right away all the doors of the prison opened, and the chains fell off all the prisoners.

es.L: Y de repente hubo un gran terremoto, de modo que fueron sacudidos los cimientos de la cárcel; y al instante se abrieron todas las puertas, y las cadenas de todos se soltaron.
es.B: De pronto se produjo un terremoto tan fuerte que la cárcel se estremeció hasta los cimientos. En ese mismo instante se abrieron todas las puertas, y a todos los presos se les soltaron las cadenas.
es.R: De repente hubo un terremoto muy fuerte. Sacudió la cárcel hasta los cimientos. Enseguida se abrieron todas las puertas de la cárcel, y a todos los presos se les cayeron las cadenas.

sw.L: Na ghafla palitokea tetemeko kuu la nchi, hata misingi ya gereza ikatikisika; na mara moja milango yote ikafunguka, na vifungo vya wote vikafunguliwa.
sw.B: Ghafla kulitokea tetemeko kubwa la nchi, kiasi kwamba gereza likatikiswa hadi misingi yake. Papo hapo milango yote ikafunguka, na minyororo ya kila mfungwa ikaachia.
sw.R: Ghafla kulitokea tetemeko kubwa la nchi. Lilitikisa gereza hadi kwenye misingi yake. Mara moja milango yote ya gereza ikafunguka, na minyororo ikaanguka kutoka kwa wafungwa wote.

decisions.choice: the earthquake: God's answer, freeing his servants
decisions.reason: Luke does not say so in words, but God frees his messengers from prison in 5:19 and 12:7-10, and an earthquake follows prayer in 4:31. Even so, Paul and Silas do not run.

decisions.choice: the chains were unfastened: came loose from what held them
decisions.reason: Chains were fixed to the walls or the stocks; the shaking loosened the fastenings.

source.text: ἔξυπνος δὲ γενόμενος ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ καὶ ἰδὼν ἀνεῳγμένας τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἤμελλεν ἑαυτὸν ἀναιρεῖν, νομίζων ἐκπεφευγέναι τοὺς δεσμίους.

records.literal_gloss: Awake then having become the jailer and having seen opened the doors of the prison, having drawn the sword he was about himself to kill, supposing to have escaped the prisoners.

en.L: And the jailer, waking up and seeing the doors of the prison opened, drew [his] sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.
en.B: Startled out of sleep, the jailer saw that the prison doors stood open. Believing that the prisoners had got away, he drew his sword, ready to take his own life.
en.R: The jailer woke up and saw that the doors of the prison were open. He thought the prisoners had run away. So he pulled out his sword to kill himself.

es.L: Y el carcelero, despertándose y viendo abiertas las puertas de la cárcel, sacando la espada, iba a matarse, pensando que los presos se habían escapado.
es.B: El carcelero despertó sobresaltado y vio abiertas las puertas de la cárcel. Creyendo que los presos se habían escapado, sacó la espada, dispuesto a quitarse la vida.
es.R: El carcelero se despertó y vio que las puertas de la cárcel estaban abiertas. Pensó que los presos se habían escapado. Entonces sacó su espada para matarse.

sw.L: Na mlinzi wa gereza, akiamka na kuona milango ya gereza imefunguliwa, aliuchomoa upanga [wake], akawa karibu kujiua, akidhani kwamba wafungwa wamekimbia.
sw.B: Mlinzi wa gereza aliamka kwa mshtuko, akaona milango ya gereza iko wazi. Akidhani kwamba wafungwa wametoroka, akauchomoa upanga wake, tayari kujiua.
sw.R: Mlinzi wa gereza aliamka, akaona kwamba milango ya gereza ilikuwa wazi. Alidhani kwamba wafungwa walikuwa wamekimbia. Basi akauchomoa upanga wake ili ajiue.

decisions.choice: about to kill himself: he expected to die for the escape
decisions.reason: A guard who let prisoners escape could suffer the penalty they would have suffered (12:19, 27:42). The jailer chose death by his own hand over trial and disgrace.

decisions.choice: supposing: he assumed it, without looking
decisions.reason: In the dark he saw the open doors and drew the obvious conclusion.

source.text: ἐφώνησεν δὲ φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Παῦλος λέγων· Μηδὲν πράξῃς σεαυτῷ κακόν, ἅπαντες γάρ ἐσμεν ἐνθάδε.

records.literal_gloss: Called out but with a voice loud the Paul saying, Nothing do to yourself harm, all for we are here.

en.L: But Paul called out with a loud voice, saying, "Do yourself no harm, for we are all here."
en.B: But Paul shouted at the top of his voice, "Do not hurt yourself! Every one of us is still here!"
en.R: But Paul shouted loudly, "Do not hurt yourself! We are all still here!"

es.L: Pero Pablo gritó con gran voz, diciendo: «No te hagas ningún mal, porque todos estamos aquí».
es.B: Pero Pablo le gritó con todas sus fuerzas: «¡No te hagas daño! ¡Todos estamos todavía aquí!».
es.R: Pero Pablo gritó muy fuerte: «¡No te hagas daño! ¡Todos seguimos aquí!».

sw.L: Lakini Paulo aliita kwa sauti kuu, akisema, "Usijidhuru hata kidogo, kwa maana sisi sote tuko hapa."
sw.B: Lakini Paulo alipaza sauti kwa nguvu zake zote, "Usijidhuru! Sisi sote bado tuko hapa!"
sw.R: Lakini Paulo alipiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa, "Usijiumize! Sote bado tuko hapa!"

decisions.choice: all: all the prisoners, not only Paul and Silas
decisions.reason: The jailer feared that the prisoners had escaped (16:27). Paul tells him none has. Luke does not say why the others stayed.

decisions.choice: do yourself no harm: a command not to go through with it
decisions.reason: The aorist with "no" forbids an act about to be done.

decisions.choice: still here
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that no one had left.

source.text: αἰτήσας δὲ φῶτα εἰσεπήδησεν καὶ ἔντρομος γενόμενος προσέπεσεν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ, καὶ προαγαγὼν αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἔφη· Κύριοι, τί με δεῖ ποιεῖν ἵνα σωθῶ;

records.literal_gloss: Having asked for then lights he rushed in, and trembling having become he fell down before the Paul and the Silas, \v 30 and having brought them outside he was saying, Sirs, what me is it necessary to do that I may be saved?

en.L: And asking for lights, he rushed in, and becoming terrified, he fell down before Paul and Silas, \v 30 and bringing them outside, he said, "Sirs, what must I do that I may be saved?"
